 Judgment

This claim petition under Section 166 Motor Vehicles Act 1989 is filed by the petitioners seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- for the death of Kum.Ganvitha R D/o Ramesh S.T. in a road traffic accident.

2. The petitioners, who are the parents of the deceased Ganvitha, have stated that on 10.12.2023 at about 10.30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider along with her aunt on a two-wheeler bearing registration No. No.KA-51-HW-3038 near Sarjapura Bus Stand, Ittanguru Circle, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District.

At that time, the driver of a tipper lorry bearing registration No. Reg.No..KA-59-6437 (hereinafter referred to as the "alleged offending vehicle") drove in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the two-wheeler of the deceased.
3. As a result of the collision, the deceased fell and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately shifted to Sri Spandana Hospital, where she received medical treatment.

Despite best medical care,
the deceased succumbed to her injuries on 14.12.2023 at 8.18 p.m.
Post-mortem examination was conducted at Oxford Hospital, and the dead body was handed over to the petitioners, who performed the funeral and other obsequies at a cost exceeding Rs. 2,00,000/-.
4. At the time of the accident, the deceased was a healthy student and was actively helping her parents and siblings in household affairs.
The petitioners have stated that the untimely death of Ganvitha has caused them immense mental shock, agony, and emotional trauma.
5. It is further contended that the accident and the resultant death of Ganvitha occurred solely due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle.
The petitioners have therefore prayed for award of compensation from Respondent No. 1 and Respondent No. 2, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, respectively.
6. Respondent No. 1, the insurer of the alleged offending vehicle, appeared before the Tribunal through its counsel and filed a written statement.
Respondent No. 2, the owner of the offending vehicle, did not appear and was accordingly placed exparte.

However, Respondent No.1, in its written objections, has admitted the issuance of an insurance policy in favour of the offending vehicle, but has contended that its liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of the said policy.

7. It is contended on behalf of the respondent no.1 that the owner of the offending vehicle failed to comply with the mandatory provisions of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of the Motor Vehicles Act regarding intimation to the police.

It is further alleged that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the rider of the two-wheeler, who was riding recklessly as a pillion rider and was not Ramesh S T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68262239/

sentences.text: wearing a helmet or in possession of a valid driving licence.
Respondent No. 1 also contended that the driver of the offending vehicle did not hold a valid driving licence at the relevant time.
8. Further, the respondent No.1 has disputed the age, as well as the relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
They have also contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is excessive.
On these grounds, the respondent has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

9. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that Ganvitha R. D/o.Ramesh S.T. died in a Road Traffic accident occurred on 10- 12-2023 at about 10.30 a.m. near Sarjapura Bus stand, Ittanguru circle, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Lorry bearing reg.No.KA-59-6437?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount?
3. What order or award ?
10. The father of the deceased was examined as PW.1 and 16 documents were got marked as Exs.P.1 to P.15.
On the other hand the Respondent no 1 has not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.
11. Having heard the counsel for both sides and have perused the material on record.

12. After hearing arguments of both parties and considering the available evidence and material on record, My findings to the above issues are as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 13. ISSUE NO.1:-

The petitioner stated that on 10-12-2023 at about 10:30 a.m., the deceased was proceeding as a pillion rider along with her aunt on a two-wheeler bearing registration number KA-51-HW- 3038 near Sarjapura Ittanguru Circle, Sarjapura Hobli, Anekal Taluk, Bengaluru District.
At that time, the driver of the offending vehicle drove in a rash and negligent manner and collided with the two-wheeler of the deceased.
As a result of the collision, the deceased fell and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately shifted to Shri Spandana Hospital, where she received medical treatment.
Despite best medical care, the deceased succumbed to her injuries on 14- 12-2023 at 8:18 p.m.

sentences.text: On the other hand, the respondent insurance company denied negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

They contended that the accident occurred solely due to the negligence of the rider of the two-wheeler, who was allegedly riding recklessly as a pillion rider, not wearing a helmet, and did not possess a valid driving license.

15. PW-1 relied on police documents exhibited as P-1 to P-9 and P-11, including the FIR, FIS,
Inquest Report, Post-Mortem Report, IMV Report, Rough Sketch, MLC, Charge Sheet, Death Summary, and other relevant records.
These documents indicate negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

16. Although the respondent insurance company contended that the accident occurred solely due to the rider's negligence, during cross-examination, PW-1 stated that the two-wheeler rider allegedly lost control of the vehicle due to high speed.
The respondent argued that the scooter did not have a valid and effective insurance, and to claim compensation, the offending vehicle was falsely implicated.

17. The petitioner, however, argued that after thorough investigation, the police filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, establishing the involvement of the offending vehicle in causing the accident.
The deceased sustained injuries solely due to the collision with the offending tipper lorry.

18. Upon careful examination of the material on record and the arguments of both parties, it is observed that, except for suggestions raised during cross-examination, the respondent insurance company has not produced any evidence to disprove the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
There is no material on record to contradict the petitioner's evidence.
The evidence of PW-1 is corroborated by the documents produced, and nothing has been elicited to disprove the petitioner's case.
19. Therefore, the contention raised by Respondent No.1 that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the rider of the two-wheeler holds no merit.
It is a well-settled principle that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial legislation, and the tribunal need not insist on strict proof of rash and negligent driving.
20. After investigation, the police filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle.
The contents of the charge sheet establish rash and negligent driving on the part of the offending driver.
From all the above documents, it is clear that the deceased sustained injuries in a road traffic accident solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Thus, the tribunal is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle was negligent in causing the accident, which resulted in the death of Ganvitha due to the injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
21. ISSUE NO.2:-
The petitioner stated that they are the parents of the deceased, Ganvitha..
The documents produced at Exhibits P-12 to P-15, including the family tree and Aadhaar cards of the petitioner and deceased, establish that Ganvitha. was indeed their daughter.

The Inquest Ramesh S T vs New India Ass Co Ltd on 8 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68262239/
4 Report,PM, and Charge Sheet also reveal that the names of the father and mother of the deceased are Ramesh and Uma, and the dead body was handed over to them.

sentences.text: Hence, it is held that the petitioners are the natural parents of the deceased, and as such, the legal heirs of Ganvitha., entitled to claim compensation.
22. It is stated by the petitioner that the deceased, Ganvitha., was 7 years of age at the time of the accident and was a student.
Although the petitioner did not produce documents to specifically show her education, it is clear from Exhibit P-15 (Aadhaar card) that her date of birth was 08-11-2016.
Consequently, at the time of the accident, she was about 7 years old.

23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in decision 2013 AIR SCW 5037 (Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others) has held that if the deceased is a minor, a notional income of Rs. 36,000 per annum may be considered for calculating loss of dependency.

entities.text: 2013 AIR SCW 5037 (Kishan Gopal and another Vs. Lala and others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Applying this principle, it is held that the deceased child, had she been alive, would have certainly contributed substantially to the family.
Therefore, a notional income of Rs. 36,000 per annum is just and reasonable.
24. In determining the appropriate multiplier, the age of the youngest parent of the deceased must be considered.

The petitioner has produced Aadhaar cards to prove their ages (Ex.P-13 and P-14),
showing that the father's date of birth is 26-09-1984 and the mother's date of birth is 28-03-1993.
Hence, the mother of the deceased, Uma, being the youngest parent, was aged about 30 years at the time of the accident.
25. Applying the legal principle laid down in Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation, a multiplier of 17 is appropriate.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, calculating loss of dependency: Notional income: Rs.
36,000 per annum, Multiplier: 17

Total compensation for loss of dependency: Rs. 36,000  17 = Rs.
6,12,000/-.
Hence, the total compensation payable towards loss of dependency is Rs. 6,12,000/-.
26. CONSORTIUM:

By following the guidelines of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Ors. 1, this Tribunal deems it proper to hold that the petitioners are entitled Rs.44,000/- each under the head of Filial Consortium as the petitioners have lost their daughter.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs- Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
27. Further, Hon'ble Apex Court has fixed the reasonable figure on conventional heads viz., loss of estate, funeral expenses at para.54 of the judgment reported in 2017 ACJ 2700.
28.
In the present case, petitioners have suffered loss to estate due to untimely death of deceased Ganvitha.

Taking into consideration all the said aspects, this Tribunal is of the view that it would be just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- under the head loss to estate, and Rs.16,500/- towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
Medical expenses: The accident has occurred on 10-12-2023 and deceased Ganvitha was under treatment till 14-012-2023 and died during the course of treatment.

sentences.text: 5 bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.7,26,878/-.
On perusal of medical bills it appears that the petitioners have spent Rs.7,26,878/- towards medical expense.
The bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, petitioners are entitled Rs.7,26,878/- towards medical expenses.
30. In all, the amount of compensation awarded by this Tribunal to the petitioners under various headings is as follows :
Compensation
heads Amount

1. Loss of dependency Rs. 6,12,000/-
2. Loss of Filial Rs. 88,000/-
 Consortium 3. Loss of estate Rs. 20,000/-
4. Transportation of dead body Rs. 16,500/-
and Funeral Expenses 5.

Medical expenses Rs. 7,26,878/-
 Total Rs. 14,63,378/-
31.
Liability:
As it is already held that the accident was only due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Respondent No.1 being the insurer and respondent No.2 being the insured of offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation.

However,
respondent No.1 is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners with interest at 6% p.a.

With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
32. ISSUE NO.3 :
In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V. Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioners are awarded compensation of Rs.14,63,378/- together with interest @ 6%
p.a. from the date of petition till the realisation.
Respondent No.1 shall deposit the aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of amount, 50% each of amount is apportioned to petitioner No.1 and 2.
After deposit of the amount, the entire amount with interest shall be through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
